label: South and South-East Asia regulators
summary: Central-bank and national-authority frameworks (State Bank of Pakistan, Pakistan's PISF, Central Bank of Sri Lanka, MAS). The regulator decides who is covered and the entity decides which provisions fit its risk, so onboarding records the entity type, the governance bodies, the critical systems or cloud workloads, and who reports incidents on which clock.

source.ref: Scope statements of the SBP, PISF, CBSL and MAS texts; each field names its own source

fields.label: SBP entity type

source.ref: SBP press release 30 May 2017 (ETGRMF scope) and the SBP cloud framework (regulated entities)

fields.note: The ETGRMF covers banks, development finance institutions and microfinance banks. The cloud framework also covers digital banks, e-money institutions and payment system operators and providers. SBP asks which one you are.

fields.label: Gap analysis
options: Done, not reviewed by the board
Done and reviewed by the board

source.ref: SBP press release 30 May 2017 on the ETGRMF (BPRD Circular 05/2017): institutions start with a gap analysis

fields.note: SBP's announcement tells institutions to start with a gap analysis against the framework. Record where it stands; the journey's controls then carry the detailed assessment.

fields.label: Gap analysis date

in: Done, not reviewed by the board
Done and reviewed by the board

source.ref: SBP press release 30 May 2017 on the ETGRMF: gap analysis first, board review at least quarterly

fields.note: Date the gap analysis was finished, so the baseline the board and SBP see can be dated.

fields.label: Applicable provisions

source.ref: SBP press release 30 May 2017 on the ETGRMF: not one-size-fits-all, each institution decides which provisions apply to its technology risk profile

fields.note: SBP calls the framework risk-based: each institution decides which provisions fit its technology risk profile. Write the decision and the reasons so the board and an SBP inspection can follow it.

fields.label: PISF entity type

source.ref: PISF 2026 documents on the nCERT site (research agent read the PDFs; document list re-checked)

fields.note: PISF applies to federal and provincial ministries and departments, autonomous bodies, corporations, CERTs and designated critical information infrastructure. It does not cover banks as such: choose Other if none fits, and ask the issuing authority.

fields.label: CII status

source.ref: PISF 2026 documents on the nCERT site: conditional CII Protection module

fields.note: PISF adds a 37-control module for designated critical information infrastructure. Designation comes from the authority, not from the organisation: if unsure, ask the sector regulator.

fields.label: Conditional modules

source.ref: PISF 2026 documents on the nCERT site: conditional modules Data Centre, Secure SDLC, CII Protection

fields.note: Three modules apply only in some cases: Data Centre (34 controls), Secure SDLC (10) and CII Protection (37), counted within PISF's 234 controls. Pick those that apply to the entity.

fields.label: Notified version

source.ref: PISF 2026 notification date and Gazette status could not be confirmed: reported as 13 Oct 2026 (approval 10 Aug 2026) while the nCERT page upload paths read 2026/03

fields.note: The PISF text and notification the entity works to. The notification date and Gazette status of PISF 2026 could not be confirmed (unverified); copy them from the nCERT page.

fields.label: Sri Lanka entity

source.ref: CBSL Banking Act Directions No. 16 of 2021 on technology risk and resilience (licensed banks)

fields.note: Banking Act Directions No. 16 of 2021 is the current technology risk instrument for licensed banks; whether it supersedes the Baseline Security Standard is unverified. A finance company should confirm with CBSL which direction binds it.

fields.label: D-SIB status

source.ref: CBSL Banking Act Directions No. 16 of 2021: D-SIBs and other licensed banks are treated differently

fields.note: The Directions treat domestic systemically important banks (D-SIBs) differently from other licensed banks. Say which group the bank is in; CBSL can confirm it.

fields.label: MAS entity type

source.ref: MAS Notice FSM-N05 (banks) and the MAS Technology Risk Management Guidelines (January 2021)

fields.note: Notice FSM-N05 is the technology risk notice for banks; the Guidelines are issued to financial institutions generally. Other institutions should confirm with MAS which notice binds them.

fields.label: Notices followed

source.ref: MAS Notices FSM-N05 and FSM-N06, both effective 10 May 2024; Notice 655 status page (cancelled 10 May 2024)

fields.note: Notice 655 was cancelled on 10 May 2024 and replaced by FSM-N06; Notice 644 was replaced by FSM-N05 the same day. Do not cite the cancelled numbers.

source.ref: PISF 2026 documents on the nCERT site: eight-parameter maturity score (0 to 3 each, maximum 24), tiers and implementation periods (research agent read the PDFs; document list re-checked)

fields.label: Parameter 1
fields.note: Score 0 to 3 for the first of PISF's eight maturity parameters (the total can reach 24). Take the parameter's name and scoring guide from the PISF documents.

fields.label: Parameter 2
fields.note: Score 0 to 3 for the second maturity parameter. Same scale and same source as above.

fields.label: Parameter 3
fields.note: Score 0 to 3 for the third maturity parameter.

fields.label: Parameter 4
fields.note: Score 0 to 3 for the fourth maturity parameter.

fields.label: Parameter 5
fields.note: Score 0 to 3 for the fifth maturity parameter.

fields.label: Parameter 6
fields.note: Score 0 to 3 for the sixth maturity parameter.

fields.label: Parameter 7
fields.note: Score 0 to 3 for the seventh maturity parameter.

fields.label: Parameter 8
fields.note: Score 0 to 3 for the eighth maturity parameter.

fields.label: Maturity tier
fields.note: Add the eight scores: a total of 0 to 8 is Tier 1 Foundational, 9 to 16 is Tier 2 Developing, 17 to 24 is Tier 3 Established. Choose the tier your total gives; PISF also attaches minimum capability conditions to the tiers.

fields.label: Conditions checked
fields.note: Tick when each minimum capability condition of the chosen tier was checked against the entity. A score alone may not qualify for a tier.

fields.label: Start date
fields.note: Date the implementation period starts. PISF sets 12, 15 or 18 months depending on the tier; read which period belongs to your tier in the PISF documents.

fields.label: Target date
fields.note: Date the implementation period ends: the start date plus the 12, 15 or 18 months that apply to the tier.

source.ref: Governance expectations in the SBP, PISF, CBSL and MAS texts; each field names its own source

fields.label: Board IT committee

source.ref: SBP ETGRMF (BPRD Circular 05/2017): the circular text could not be read, so this expectation is assumed from later SBP frameworks

fields.note: Later SBP frameworks assume a board committee that oversees IT and technology risk. Whether the ETGRMF itself requires one is unverified; SBP decides what it expects of each institution.

fields.label: IT steering committee

source.ref: SBP ETGRMF (BPRD Circular 05/2017): the circular text could not be read, so this expectation is assumed from later SBP frameworks

fields.note: A management committee that steers IT and security work. Later SBP frameworks assume one; whether the ETGRMF requires it is unverified because its text could not be read.

fields.label: Board review

source.ref: SBP press release 30 May 2017 on the ETGRMF: the board reviews at least quarterly

fields.note: SBP's announcement says the board reviews the framework at least quarterly. Record how often it reviews today.

fields.label: Security lead

source.ref: SBP ETGRMF (BPRD Circular 05/2017): the circular text could not be read, so this expectation is assumed from later SBP frameworks

fields.note: The named head of information security. The ETGRMF text could not be read, so what SBP requires of this role is unverified; later SBP frameworks assume a named lead.

fields.label: Lead independent

source.ref: SBP ETGRMF (BPRD Circular 05/2017): the circular text could not be read, so this expectation is assumed from later SBP frameworks

fields.note: Tick when the security lead does not report to the head of IT. Whether SBP requires this is unverified because the ETGRMF text could not be read.

fields.label: Board approval

source.ref: SBP ETGRMF (BPRD Circular 05/2017): the circular text could not be read, so this expectation is assumed from later SBP frameworks

fields.note: Date the board approved the technology governance framework or the plan to meet it. Unverified: the ETGRMF text could not be read, so whether SBP asks for an approval date is not confirmed.

fields.label: Board approval

source.ref: SBP Regulations for the Security of Internet Banking (Payment Systems Department)

fields.note: Date the board approved the internet banking security framework. SBP's regulation requires a board-approved security framework.

fields.label: Risk assessment

source.ref: SBP Regulations for the Security of Internet Banking (Payment Systems Department)

fields.note: Date of the latest documented security risk assessment for internet banking. The regulation asks for one and for it to be refreshed at least annually.

fields.label: Cloud policy

source.ref: SBP Framework on Outsourcing to Cloud Service Providers (BPRD Circular 01/2023)

fields.note: Date the board approved the cloud policy. SBP's cloud framework requires a board-approved policy.

fields.label: Accountable head

source.ref: PISF 2026 documents on the nCERT site: governance prerequisites

fields.note: The head of the organisation, who is accountable for PISF compliance. PISF lists this among its governance prerequisites.

fields.label: Steering committee

source.ref: PISF 2026 documents on the nCERT site: governance prerequisites

fields.note: PISF lists a formally notified steering committee among its governance prerequisites. Say where yours stands.

fields.label: Security lead

source.ref: PISF 2026 documents on the nCERT site: governance prerequisites

fields.note: The head of the security function. PISF expects a security function that is independent of IT.

fields.label: Independent of IT

source.ref: PISF 2026 documents on the nCERT site: governance prerequisites

fields.note: Tick when the security function does not report to the head of IT. PISF lists an independent security function as a governance prerequisite.

fields.label: Budget

source.ref: PISF 2026 documents on the nCERT site: governance prerequisites

fields.note: PISF lists a budget among its governance prerequisites. Record whether funds for implementation are approved.

fields.label: RACI defined

source.ref: PISF 2026 documents on the nCERT site: governance prerequisites

fields.note: Tick when roles for the PISF work are assigned in a RACI (responsible, accountable, consulted, informed). PISF lists it among its prerequisites.

fields.label: ISC chair

source.ref: CBSL Banking Act Directions No. 16 of 2021 on technology risk and resilience

fields.note: Chair of the Information Security Committee. The Directions require the committee to be chaired by the CEO.

fields.label: CEO chairs ISC

source.ref: CBSL Banking Act Directions No. 16 of 2021 on technology risk and resilience

fields.note: Tick when the chair named above is the CEO, as the Directions require.

fields.label: CISO

source.ref: CBSL Banking Act Directions No. 16 of 2021 on technology risk and resilience

fields.note: The chief information security officer. The Directions place the CISO within two layers below the CEO.

fields.label: CISO level

source.ref: CBSL Banking Act Directions No. 16 of 2021 on technology risk and resilience

fields.note: The Directions put the CISO within two layers below the CEO. Say which layer the CISO sits in today.

fields.label: CIO

source.ref: MAS Technology Risk Management Guidelines (January 2021): board, CIO and CISO expectations

fields.note: The chief information officer or head of technology. The Guidelines set expectations for the board, the CIO and the CISO; name both roles.

fields.label: CISO

source.ref: MAS Technology Risk Management Guidelines (January 2021): board, CIO and CISO expectations

fields.note: The chief information security officer. The Guidelines set expectations for this role; name the person who holds it.

fields.label: Roles approved

source.ref: MAS TRM Guidelines (January 2021) set CIO and CISO expectations; the CEO-approval detail comes from the plan's design and was not located in the text

fields.note: Date the CEO approved the responsibilities of the CIO and CISO. Unverified: the Guidelines set expectations for these roles, but a CEO sign-off date is not confirmed as a MAS requirement.

fields.label: Appetite approved

source.ref: MAS Technology Risk Management Guidelines (January 2021): board and senior management oversight

fields.note: Date the board approved the technology risk appetite. The Guidelines expect board and senior management oversight of technology risk.

source.ref: Critical-system and workload rules in the SBP, PISF, CBSL and MAS texts; each field names its own source

fields.label: Critical systems

source.ref: SBP press release 30 May 2017 on the ETGRMF: risk-based, each institution decides what fits its technology risk profile

fields.note: Systems the institution treats as critical to its technology risk profile. SBP leaves risk-based choices to each institution, so the list is yours to justify.

fields.label: Internet banking systems

source.ref: SBP Regulations for the Security of Internet Banking (Payment Systems Department)

fields.note: Systems that deliver internet banking: portal, authentication, links to core banking. The security framework and the risk assessment are written against them.

fields.label: No cloud workloads

source.ref: SBP Framework on Outsourcing to Cloud Service Providers (BPRD Circular 01/2023)

fields.note: Tick when no workload runs with a cloud service provider, so an empty list is a decision and not an omission.

fields.label: Cloud workloads

source.ref: SBP Framework on Outsourcing to Cloud Service Providers (BPRD Circular 01/2023)

fields.note: One row per cloud workload. The institution classifies each as material or non-material; offshore material workloads need SBP approval and material workloads need one month's prior notice to SBP.

fields.label: CII systems

source.ref: PISF 2026 documents on the nCERT site: CII Protection module

fields.note: The systems that make up the designated critical information infrastructure. The CII Protection module of 37 controls applies to this infrastructure.

fields.label: Data centre sites

source.ref: PISF 2026 documents on the nCERT site: Data Centre module

fields.note: Sites that host data centre equipment. The Data Centre module of 34 controls applies where the entity runs one.

fields.label: Board identified

source.ref: CBSL Banking Act Directions No. 16 of 2021 on technology risk and resilience

fields.note: Tick when the Board has identified the critical information systems. The Directions put that decision with the Board.

fields.label: Critical systems

source.ref: CBSL Banking Act Directions No. 16 of 2021 on technology risk and resilience

fields.note: The critical information systems the Board identified, picked from the key systems in the organisation profile.

fields.label: System register

source.ref: CBSL Banking Act Directions No. 16 of 2021 on technology risk and resilience

fields.note: The Directions call for a register of all information systems. Record how far yours is; a partial register is accepted at onboarding.

fields.label: Critical systems

source.ref: MAS Notice FSM-N05 and Technology Risk Management Guidelines (January 2021): critical systems, 4-hour downtime and recovery limits

fields.note: Systems whose failure would seriously disrupt services. MAS sets 4-hour limits on downtime and recovery time for a critical system, so each row records whether recovery fits.

fields.label: Outsourcing register

source.ref: MAS Notice 658 on outsourcing (11 Dec 2024), seen in secondary sources only, and the TRM Guidelines' third-party expectations

fields.note: A register of outsourced and third-party arrangements. The Guidelines set third-party expectations and Notice 658 covers outsourcing; treat the Notice detail as secondary until read at MAS.

source.ref: Incident-reporting and testing expectations in the SBP, PISF, CBSL and MAS texts; each field names its own source

fields.label: SBP contact

source.ref: SBP internet banking regulation (quarterly breach reports) and SBP cloud framework (notice of adverse developments within two working days)

fields.note: Person who files reports with SBP and receives its queries: quarterly breach reports for internet banking and notice of adverse cloud developments within two working days.

fields.label: Last breach report

source.ref: SBP Regulations for the Security of Internet Banking (Payment Systems Department)

fields.note: Date of the latest quarterly breach report to SBP. Leave empty if none has been filed yet.

fields.label: Contingency test

source.ref: SBP Framework on Outsourcing to Cloud Service Providers (BPRD Circular 01/2023)

fields.note: Date of the latest contingency test of cloud workloads. SBP's cloud framework asks for a test every year.

fields.label: Provider audit

source.ref: SBP Framework on Outsourcing to Cloud Service Providers (BPRD Circular 01/2023)

fields.note: Date of the latest audit of the cloud provider. SBP asks for an audit every two years for material workloads.

fields.label: PISF contact

source.ref: PISF 2026 documents on the nCERT site

fields.note: Person who reports incidents under PISF. The receiving body and the report clocks must be read from the PISF documents; see Report clocks.

fields.label: Report clocks

source.ref: PISF incident report clocks (72 and 120 hours) appear only in working notes and could not be confirmed in the PISF documents

fields.note: Hours allowed for the first and the full incident report under PISF. Working notes mention 72 and 120 hours; this is unverified, so copy the figures from the notified text.

fields.label: CBSL contact

source.ref: CBSL Bank Supervision Department circular No. 2 of 2025 (incident reporting)

fields.note: Person who files incident reports with CBSL. Circular No. 2 of 2025 sets reporting at 2 hours, 14 days and quarterly.

fields.label: MAS contact

source.ref: MAS Notice FSM-N05 (effective 10 May 2024): incident notification and root-cause report

fields.note: Person who notifies MAS of incidents. MAS requires notification within 1 hour and a root-cause report within 14 days.

fields.label: Next pen test

fields.note: Date of the next independent penetration test. Regulators and assessors ask for the latest test and the plan; past tests belong in the audit history of the organisation profile.

fields.label: Next audit

source.ref: Penetration-test and audit dates as regulators and assessors ask for them; the MAS TRM Guidelines cover cyber security assessment and IT audit, other frameworks follow common practice

fields.note: Date of the next independent audit or assurance review against this framework. Past audits belong in the audit history of the organisation profile.
